subject: Dedicated capacity for DeepField - traffic snapshot request
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@deepfield.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@deepfield.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity for DeepField - traffic snapshot request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the intro — we spoke with your website sign-up and would like to explore a Dedicated capacity engagement for DeepField.ai. We run a multi-tenant inference layer that powers our developer-facing API (document summarization + retrieval augmented generation pipelines). Before a sizing call, our infra team exported a short telemetry slice so your pre-sales team can get a head start.

Quick context: we expect production ramp starting Q1 2027 with an initial GA cohort of ~4 customers, and broader rollouts in Q2. Primary needs are predictable p99 latencies for short chat-style prompts and the ability to sustain bursts during peak business hours.

Can you send your pre-sales questionnaire or a short checklist so we can fill in the traffic/concurrency details? Attached a 48-hour sample (sanitized).

Attachments: [Attachment: initial_telemetry_export.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)]

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Director of Infrastructure, DeepField.ai
alex@deepfield.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@deepfield.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for DeepField - traffic snapshot request

Alex — thanks for sending the sample. Looping in Marissa (solutions lead) and Vivek (capacity planning). I attached a concise questionnaire that helps us produce a deterministic fleet projection (we try to avoid back-and-forth on basic telemetry). If you can return most of these fields we can run an initial node-count / SKU recommendation and a shortworkshop to validate.
High-level items we need (short checklist):
- Traffic profile: baseline QPS, 95th/99th peak QPS, and expected growth over 3 months.
- Prompt/response token distribution: typical prompt tokens, typical generated tokens, percent of streaming responses.
- Sessionization: do you use session affinity / persistent KV cache per user, or stateless calls?
- Concurrency targets: target p50/p95/p99 latency SLOs and acceptable queueing window.
- Model family & quantization: model(s) you plan to serve (e.g., Llama2-70B-INT8) and whether you accept quantized variants.
- Caching & reuse: percent of requests eligible for prefix/KV cache reuse.
- Burst multipliers: expected burst factor (x baseline) and typical burst duration.
- Security/region constraints: any VPC/on-prem requirements, KMS/HSM needs, data residency.

Attachments I sent: [Attachment: rachel_questionnaire.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)], [Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizer-guide.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

If you prefer, we can run through this in a 30-minute call; Marissa — are you available tomorrow morning PST for a 30-min sizing workshop?

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex@deepfield.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@deepfield.ai, procurement@deepfield.ai
Date: 2026-11-26T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for DeepField - traffic snapshot request

Rachel / team — thanks for the questionnaire. Answers below (pulled from the 48h export + product roadmap). Let me know if you want raw traces.

- Baseline QPS: 45 QPS sustained (US-west region).
- Peak QPS (95/99): 120 QPS (95th), 210 QPS (99th) over short bursts.
- Growth: expecting ~30% month-over-month during Q1 ramp.
- Prompt tokens (median): 18 tokens.
- Generation tokens (median): 62 tokens. Tail (95th gen tokens): 340 tokens.
- Streaming: ~28% of calls prefer streaming.
- Sessionization: we maintain short-lived sessions with per-session KV caches (avg session length 3 requests, TTL 120s).
- Concurrency targets / SLOs: p50 40ms, p95 120ms, p99 250ms for non-streaming; streaming p50/p95: 120ms/300ms first-byte. Acceptable queueing window: up to 800ms for brief bursts.
- Models: planning to use a quantized Llama2-70B variant (INT8/4-bit experimental) and an Llama2-13B for lower-latency routes.
- Caching: we estimate ~12% prefix reuse for our most common flows.
- Burst profile: typical burst multiplier x5 for 60-300s; rare megaburst x10 for <60s during product launches.
- Security: US-only region, VPC peering, KMS integration required.

Attachments: [Attachment: df_telemetry_sample.csv (CSV, 1.9MB)]

Happy to hop on a call; Marissa — tomorrow 10:00 PST works for us.

— Alex

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex@deepfield.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity for DeepField - traffic snapshot request

Folks — forwarding DeepField's answers. Key signals: baseline 45 QPS, 99th bursts to 210 QPS, median gen tokens ~62 with 95th at 340, ~28% streaming, session affinity with short KV TTL. US-only + KMS.

Initial ask: can we run a quick capacity projection under two occupancy assumptions (conservative 40% occupancy, and optimistic 60%) and map to SKUs we typically propose (g5-4x, g5-8x, and an a100-equivalent host)? Please include:
- Node count per SKU for steady-state and peak burst headroom.
- Expected per-token cost estimate (hosted vs dedicated delta).
- Recommended caching/batching configs to hit p95/p99 with <800ms queueing.

Marissa — can you put a short slide with a recommended starting pack (commit) + canary headroom for the 30-day ramp? Vivek — any special notes on our quantized Llama2-70B throughput assumptions I should call out ahead of the call?

Attachments: [Attachment: deal_brief_deepfield.pdf (PDF, 58KB)]

— Rachel
